tweets.author: comrade-letrinhan.bsky.social
tweets.text: This is hilarious, but I'd genuinely love to see a benchmark. I simulated 10 million Bitcoin traders making random decisions, and some posted absurd returns without any skill. Fly-brain trading versus random trading, after fees, would be a great comparison.

tweets.author: comrade-letrinhan.bsky.social
tweets.text: Building the system in six days is impressive. Calling it competitive is the part I'd want to test. I simulated 10 million random Bitcoin traders and found extraordinary winners with zero skill. How was the system benchmarked after costs?

tweets.author: comrade-letrinhan.bsky.social
tweets.text: Congrats on getting it through four revisions. I like the emphasis on a simple baseline for Bitcoin forecasting. Did the results hold up across different test periods, or were they sensitive to where you made the train/test split?

tweets.author: fulcrumenterprises.bsky.social
tweets.text: Of those, only the Bitcoin proof needs no issuer at all. The two TSA timestamps still lean on each authority's certificate chain, and the DOI on Zenodo staying up. Does your checker report which layer failed, or just pass or fail overall?

tweets.author: comrade-letrinhan.bsky.social
tweets.text:
How are they even measuring the performance of a top 10% Jane Street trader?

I simulated 10 million random Bitcoin traders and some produced extraordinary returns purely by chance. Without a proper out-of-sample comparison, claims like this don't tell us much.
